answer: Vine nodes in many cities ping every seat's quartz chip, which signs each reply, and record the round-trip times. Seats whose latency fingerprints match within 2 ms count as one site, and the k-th seat at a site must lock k² voyage to vote. An honest newcomer on its own machine locks 1 voyage. An operator running 100 clones in one rack locks 338,350 voyage, or must lease hardware in 100 distant cities, each with its own quartz chip answering the vine.
